commit.message: feat(loop-closure): loop watcher — counter-metrics, ingestion, canary duty

intent: PR-F of the walking-mode loop-closure plan: read-only watcher over lane PRs (test-deletion-without-signoff, required-contexts-actually-reported on the head SHA, tier-2 touches, diff sanity), ingestion of operator comments from the pinned walking-brief issue into mailbox tasks on the loop-tasks branch (create-only, owner-authored comments only), and the weekly seeded-canary duty with canary PRs structurally unmergeable by the unattended lane.

negative_controls.command: python3 -c "import subprocess,sys; from pathlib import Path; p=Path('scripts/governance/loop_watcher.py'); orig=p.read_text(); mut=orig.replace('tier-2 referee paths touched', 'DISABLED-finding'); assert mut!=orig; p.write_text(mut); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','tests/test_loop_watcher.py','-q'],check=False); p.write_text(orig); sys.exit(0 if r.returncode!=0 else 2)"
negative_controls.name: dropping-tier2-watch-breaks-contract-test

honest_blockers: The watcher reads the tier-2 list from scripts/governance/automerge_tier_policy.json, which lands with PR-A; on a checkout without it the tier-2 check raises and the run fails loudly rather than silently skipping.
Ingestion writes to the loop-tasks branch and echoes on the pinned issue; both exist only after PR-B/PR-C land and the first watcher run creates the branch if absent.
Reviewer-rotation changes on canary failure are Tier 2 and deliberately not automated; the watcher only reports.

Canary PRs are unmergeable by the unattended lane via the canary-sandbox hard-fail in PR-A's guard plus the mike-watch-only label; a reviewer approving one is a reported integrity failure, not a merge risk.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the single commit: watcher, workflow, and tests disappear. loop-tasks branch content and any open canary PRs remain inert artifacts the operator can delete.
